clue.text: Shocking cost in bombs, one way or another?

parts.note: something shocking is dire, dreadful

indicators.note: to bomb is to go badly wrong, so these letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that an outrageous sum was spent on bombs, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombs' looks like the weapons being paid for, but it is the anagram signal: the letters fail and fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions are routes or bearings, so each one is a way, and the question mark admits the plural fits loosely.

clue.text: White bird in alcohol, less cold

definitions.note: a white wine; the definition is an adjective used as a noun

indicators.note: the bird's name sits inside the drink's slang name
less means the cold letter is subtracted from the drink

parts.note: sauce is slang for strong drink, as in 'on the sauce'
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A white seabird floating in a drink that is not quite so chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like the bird's colour but is a wine; 'less' removes the cold letter before 'in' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux, so naming it by its colour is a fair shorthand.

clue.text: Bind private parts for Reading resident, say

indicators.note: the private word parts the tie word, splitting it open to sit inside

parts.note: to bind is to tie
something private is one's own

explanation.surface: Reads like a bawdy instruction about tying up someone's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' is a verb: OWN parts TIE. Reading is an English town, not the activity; the capital R is hidden at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in a town such as Reading, a large town west of London, is a town-dweller in slang terms.

clue.text: Original theme song for a fantasy drama

indicators.note: original means freshly invented, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Talks of writing a new theme tune for a fantasy television series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' rearranges the thirteen letters of THEME SONG FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: The HBO television series of dragons and warring houses, based on George R. R. Martin's novels, is a fantasy drama.

clue.text: With hairy part for all to see, the majority longed to conceal it

indicators.note: the majority word hides the for-all-to-see letter, which 'it' refers back to

parts.note: the majority is most of something
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences
to have longed is to have ached

explanation.surface: Something hairy on show while most people secretly wished to hide it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for all to see' is the British 'universal' film rating; 'to conceal it' hides that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporting facial hair on the upper lip has a hairy part, so the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Queen finally seen off after struggle, as was Marie Antoinette

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the struggle word

parts.note: to struggle or compete is to vie

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it
off means bad or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen is finally seen off after a struggle, as befell Marie Antoinette at the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen off' reads as killed, fitting the queen, but 'off' is the anagram signal for NNESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette was born in Vienna as an Austrian archduchess, so she was a native of that city.

clue.text: In audition, character does well

definitions.note: well as a mild exclamation of disappointment

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: the character O, the letter, and does, female deer

explanation.surface: An actor's character performs well at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: O, a written character, and DEER, which does are, sound like the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of mild dismay, said when something has gone slightly wrong.

clue.text: Blade struck four Samurai warriors, all down below

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of each word is its last letter, so each word gives its final letter

explanation.surface: A blade struck four samurai, who all fell down below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all down below' takes the last letters of struck, four, Samurai and warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay or Indonesian dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Presently, sleazeball has love for sweetheart

parts.note: 'in a mo', short for in a moment, means presently
a sleazeball is a rat, a despicable person
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Before long, a sleazy man will have love for his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, from Italian, so a sweetheart.

clue.text: Divine fluid Christian initially snubbed, Church claimed

indicators.note: the shortened name takes and holds the church letters within it
the initial letter of the designer's surname is cut

parts.note: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A Christian is snubbed while the Church lays claim to a sacred liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially snubbed' trims DIOR (as in Christian Dior) to IOR, which 'claimed' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: Understanding English, nothing missing from notes?

indicators.note: nothing is the letter O, so each O is dropped from the notes

parts.note: two notes, the plural read as the word note twice

explanation.surface: Asks whether understanding English means nothing is missing from one's notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' gives NOTE twice; 'nothing missing from' removes each O, leaving NTE NTE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding or agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: See 23
Short stretch of shorter sentence

indicators.note: stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brief spell of a reduced prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like grammar but the surface is a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and curt, so it is short in manner.

clue.text: Instrument reading as if in Arabic, rub out answer?

indicators.note: Arabic script runs right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rub out someone is slang for to murder them

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should erase an answer about a musical instrument written in Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: MURDER plus ANS, read right to left as Arabic is, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The snare is the shallow drum with wires across its lower head, a standard percussion instrument.

clue.text: Ahead in first half of game, short moves saving time

indicators.note: the scrambled letters keep the time letter safe inside them
the letters move about into a new order
first half of takes the opening two letters of the four-letter word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team ahead in the first half of a match, with short moves running down the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' reads as leading the match, but means forward; 'moves' signals the anagram and 'saving' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions saying go straight on mean keep moving forward, directly ahead.

clue.text: Still dark, it's blocked up

indicators.note: the dark word blocks in the reversed letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a night with no moon is dark

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Complains that it is still dark because something has been blocked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works as a reversal only because this is a down clue; 'blocked' encloses. 'Still' is the definition, not a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still means not moving at all, a synonym for keeping stationary.

clue.text: A fraction high?

definitions.meaning: one divided by eight is written as a fraction, one over eight
high meaning drunk, having had one drink too many

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a figure is slightly too elevated.
explanation.walkthrough: The drunken sense is a British idiom: one drink beyond the eight a person can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for slightly drunk, and read literally it is one-eighth written as a fraction.

clue.text: Jelly kept in a row of vessels?

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
a line is a row

explanation.surface: Wonders whether jelly is kept in a row of containers.
explanation.walkthrough: A line of vases, read in reverse order from the clue, gives the petroleum jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaseline is the trade name of a petroleum jelly used on skin.

clue.text: Complaining, horse in horse sandwiches?

indicators.note: the second horse holds the other pieces between its two letters like bread

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish name for a horse
a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about horse meat turning up in horse sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: GG, nursery speak for a horse, sandwiches ROAN and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Groaning is moaning or grumbling, making noises of complaint.

clue.text: Retaining information, test is provided with content

parts.note: SAT is a standard school test

indicators.note: the provided word keeps the information letter inside it

parts.note: to be provided with food is to be fed
I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: An exam paper keeps its information while the test is supplied with material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the noun meaning material, but it is the adjective meaning happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content means feeling pleased and fulfilled, the same as being satisfied.

clue.text: Paper lies, might you say?

definitions.meaning: thin soft paper, as used for wrapping or blowing the nose
from the phrase 'a ... of lies', meaning a web of falsehoods

explanation.surface: Asks whether a newspaper is printing falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense relies on the idiom 'a tissue of lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft thin paper is called this, and a web of falsehoods is idiomatically one of lies.

clue.text: Still very popular, Italian runner's hurdling

indicators.note: the river leaps over and around the popular word, so it ends up inside

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river, a runner in crossword terms
something very popular is hot

explanation.surface: An Italian athlete, still very popular, is hurdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one taken from a film.

clue.text: Piddling in crack, intimate at first

indicators.note: the intimate word comes first, before the crack word

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend, a pal
to have a crack at something is to try it

explanation.surface: Suggests something rude about urinating into a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piddling' looks like urinating but means trivial; 'crack' is a noun for an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Piddling means trivial or meagre, a synonym for insignificantly small.

clue.text: Forward march, alas, omitted, some going backwards

indicators.note: going backwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A march is sadly left out, with some participants retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is a football position: the Egyptian striker who played for Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohamed Salah is an attacking player, a forward, for Liverpool and Egypt.

clue.text: Forget a title

definitions.meaning: to forget or fail to attend, as when you skip a meeting
the form of address for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: An instruction to overlook someone's honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip or fail to catch something is to let it go, and the word is also the courtesy title for a young woman.

clue.text: A final piece of wallpaper, endless rolls around next to Mark, he finished off layer upon layer

definitions.text: he finished off layer upon layer
definitions.note: the founder of KFC, who disposed of countless laying hens, read as if a decorator sanding coats

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit next to the punctuation word

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark

indicators.note: rolls around means tumbles about, so the letters are mixed up
the final piece of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorator hanging the last bit of wallpaper, its rolls everywhere, working through coat after coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' is anagram fodder, not a deletion signal, and 'rolls around' mixes it up. The layers are hens, not coats of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The KFC founder's business killed chickens, so hens that lay eggs were finished off by him by the thousand.

clue.text: Clever cricket shot over point

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the shot comes before the point

parts.note: the cut is a cricket stroke played square on the off side
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Praises a smart cricket stroke played over the fielder at point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like the cricket fielding position, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its older sense means sharp-witted or shrewd, like the word acute.

clue.text: Refuse kick up the backside by leader in nappies

indicators.note: the leading letter is placed beside the spur word

parts.note: a spur is a goad, a prod to make someone act

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A baby in nappies refuses, and gets a smack on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn an offer is to reject it with contempt, a synonym for declining.

clue.text: See 4
